title: Keys Out of Reach: LiteLLM's Breach and Credential-Free Agents
summary: A poisoned LiteLLM release, traced back to tokens in logs, opens a day where Anthropic proves 123 libraries crash-free, Agent Skills gets a neutral home, and Fernández-Villaverde argues AI's real bottleneck is savings and rising real rates. The deep dive covers where an agent's secrets should live: sandbox tiers, egress proxies and credential brokering in Claude Code, NVIDIA OpenShell and Google's Agent Compute Engine.
shownotes:
LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromised on PyPI and Docker: credential stealer via .pth and sitecustomize, root cause chain through tokens in logs; pin 1.106.2 and rotate secrets
Anthropic Frontier Red Team: Claude writes 180 million lines of Rocq proofs showing no crashes for 239 entry points across 123 OSS-Fuzz libraries
Agent Skills donated to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation, with security guidance on the roadmap
Fernández-Villaverde, 'Saving for the Machines': savings as AI's binding constraint, soaring real rates, and the fiscal squeeze on bystander economies
Deep dive: where an agent's secrets should live - isolation tiers, egress proxies, credential brokering and policy review in Claude Code, NVIDIA OpenShell and Google Agent Compute Engine
